result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy host values verbatim via interpolated SQL (bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation scheme stripping), while record_for_host matches with where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) — bare hostnames only. Old setting values like 'http://discourse.org' (explicitly supported per the removed site_setting_spec 'works with a http host' test) would be stored with the scheme and never match, and the migration then DELETEs the original settings, destroying recoverable config. This is verifiable entirely from the diff.

judged_text: The back-compat data migration inserts each legacy embeddable_hosts value verbatim via interpolated SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so entries the old allows_embeddable_host? explicitly matched by stripping http(s):// (e.g. 'http://discourse.org', a form the old spec 'works with a http host' proved supported) are stored with the scheme intact and never match record_for_host's where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) comparison, which only ever sees a bare hostname. Embeds from every scheme-prefixed allowlisted host raise Discourse::InvalidAccess immediately after upgrade while the rows look intact in the new admin table, and the migration's final DELETE (line 31) destroys the original setting values, leaving nothing to recover the configuration from; the specs mask this because Fabricate saves the same legacy-form values through the model's normalization.
